clues: This city sits in the Merrimack Valley in the state of Massachusetts. That valley is in the part of the land called New England.
Winters here are long and very cold, and snow is a plain fact of the season. One past winter set the mark for the most snow in a whole season.
In 1826, this town was set up to serve as a mill town. That one choice shaped all the years that came after it.
Folks call this place the birthplace of the mill age in America. Its cloth mills and big work halls changed how things were made.
Its old mill sites are now kept safe in a park. The park is run by the National Park Service of the land.
